`hooks/command-safety.sh` first refuses recognized unfiltered environment dumps independently of project policy, cwd and Git. Direct named grep permission requires proven newline records; known raw NUL reads need the literal NUL-to-newline tr conversion. Flattened or unproved producer output cannot gain permission. Known nested dumps can refuse conservatively. The project-pattern check separately rejects text matching `COMMAND_SAFETY_DENY_PATTERN`, read raw and with continuations joined, including quoted text. Nonmatching text passes only that pattern check. An absent setting applies the default systemd-run memory-cap pattern; `^$` disables only pattern matching. Missing payload readers or unreadable input warn and allow the call. Empty or invalid patterns and unavailable policy tools, settings or installed support warn and allow only the pattern check; unreadable settings or support also leave the upload-host check unavailable.

The fixed check also refuses a download a shell or interpreter runs as its program, an upload to a host `COMMAND_SAFETY_UPLOAD_HOSTS` does not list, a push to a repository operand that is neither a remote nor a remote URL, and a command with a word that names `COMMAND_SAFETY_OWNER_COMMAND` outside a grep, rg, cat or sed -n argument; that variable's exact command text passes the first three. A command those refusals pass that holds a transfer in a stage that is not plain literal argv in a plain pipeline is reported, not refused. `docs/authoring/command-safety.md` lists the forms each refusal reads, the forms that only report and the forms it does not reach.
